items.en: The ⟦0⟧ is where most tactical and strategic decisions happen. It also provides information related to these purposes, such as, weather, ⟦1⟧, land combat, naval combat, and buildings.
The Map can be divided into three subdivisions:
⟦0⟧ are the smallest subunit of the map. It is here that ⟦1⟧, weather, capitals, land combat, ⟦2⟧, and ⟦3⟧ are handled.
⟦0⟧ are the next smallest subunit of the map, where ⟦1⟧, ⟦2⟧, ⟦3⟧, and country borders are decided.
⟦0⟧ are the largest of the subdivisions, and are where naval combat and ⟦1⟧ occur.

Using different ⟦0⟧, you can alter the information presented on the map. These map modes can be activated by either clicking on the appropriate button (icon) located in the lower right corner of the main screen or by pressing the associated ⟦1⟧. Additional map modes can be revealed by clicking the arrow button.

The default map mode is a combination of the political map mode and terrain map mode from previous games. It shows the name of all the nations, with their political color. Zoomed out, mainly the nation's color is seen, however, when zooming in, the terrain becomes more and more visible, integrating both map modes into one. Air fields, naval bases, capitals, and almost any other object on the map can be seen in this mode, represented by different symbols:
⟦0⟧ are a top down picture of an airplane.

⟦0⟧ are identified by a star , which can be ⟦1⟧ if it is the nation's capital, ⟦2⟧ if it is any other nation's capital, or ⟦3⟧ if it is the capital of any of the nation's enemies. All capitals contain victory points.
⟦0⟧ are denoted by either a square , a pentagon , or a circle , depending on the value. They are named when zoomed in and follow the color scheme of capitals.
⟦0⟧ can be seen as counters or sprites on the map.

⟦0⟧ can be seen as pointers that are ⟦1⟧ if the nation is winning the battle, ⟦2⟧ if the battle is favoring neither side, or ⟦3⟧ if the nation is losing the battle, and it shows a number that summarizes how much the battle favors one side or the other.
⟦0⟧ can be seen along with navies and their missions.
⟦0⟧ can be seen flying where aircraft are in operation.
⟦0⟧ and any other state- or province-wide constructions are also visible.

⟦0⟧ will be a ⟦1⟧ outline around any demilitarized area. The only time they are used is at the beginning of the game in the Rhineland, Danzig, the Turkish Straits (requires ⟦2⟧) and Åland. An exception is the option to create demilitarized zones (DMZ) during peace conferences (requires ⟦3⟧).
Shows ⟦0⟧ relevant to naval activity, with information on naval supremacy and naval tasks.

The naval map mode consists of the world's strategic regions, with a color scheme similar to the diplomacy for states on land under it. Convoy routes are also shown here with the following color scheme:
⟦0⟧ trade routes are supply transfers to oversea units.
⟦0⟧ trade routes are resource transfers. These are imports, exports or resource transfers from non-owned oversea resources.
⟦0⟧ trade routes are resource transfers. These are imports, exports or resource transfers from owned oversea resources.
⟦0⟧ trade routes are lend lease equipment routes and international market routes.

⟦0⟧ trade routes are those that have insufficient convoys to maintain 100% efficiency. The lack of convoys is due to either a country not producing enough convoys for the demand or due to convoys being sunk by the enemy (red X's indicate the region where convoys are being sunk).
Strategic regions that have sea provinces will be highlighted with ⟦0⟧ if they are under allied naval superiority. Provinces that are striped ⟦1⟧ are out of the fleets' operational range.

Canals or any type of controlled strait are shown on this map mode, and by hovering over them it is possible to see the access permissions your country has as well as the land provinces controlling the strait (⟦0⟧ outline). Straits are also shown on the Supply Map Mode and the Resource Map mode.
The following, are the names and province control points of the straits/canals on map and their respective permissions granted to nations (depending on the relations with the strait controllers).
Shows ⟦0⟧ with information on aerial supremacy. It is automatically activated when an air base is selected.
The air map mode is, at first glance, merely a map of the strategic regions of the map. However, when at war, the regions can be highlighted with three colors:
⟦0⟧, which means the enemy has air superiority.
⟦0⟧, which means the nation or its allies has air superiority.
⟦0⟧, which means the air superiority is contested.

This map mode also shows all of the air missions currently set with the total number of planes assigned. In the strategic air map mode more ground crews can be assigned, by clicking the icon in the desired strategic region. This gives a ⟦0⟧ bonus to mission efficiency in the strategic region.
Shows the operatives, their missions, on-going operations, and intel network spread. See ⟦0⟧ for more detail.
The supply map mode shows the supply network for a nation, its territories, and its allies' territories. Reference ⟦0⟧ for more detail regarding supply.

The terrain map mode shows the ⟦0⟧ of each region on the map using simplified colors. Land terrain has high adjusters for attack, defense and movement of land units while ⟦1⟧ has different adjusters for attack, defense and movement of naval units. The terrain map mode can be useful to plan your offense or defense using favorable terrain.
⟦0⟧: Light grayish with a bit yellow or green

The resistance map mode shows resistance per state. Yellow indicates low, orange higher and red high resistance. The percentage of resistance (0%-100%) is shown for each state. A green arrow downwards shows decreasing resistance, a red arrow upwards increasing resistance. Also 4 resistance tiers are shown:
Shows compliance per state. Lighter blue means more compliance. The percentage of compliance (0%-100%) is shown for each state. Also 5 compliance tiers are shown:
Shows resource locations and trade routes.

The resources map mode shows any convoy/ trade routes that are connected to the nation and canals/ straits across the world, similar to the naval map mode. However, this map mode looks like the default map mode when zoomed out, but when zoomed in, it shows a resource icon above any state that has a resource, along with the number of that resource produced in that state.
The diplomacy map mode shows its information through a multitude of colors.
⟦0⟧ is the color that any land owned and controlled by the nation
⟦0⟧ is the color that any land occupied by the nation will be colored.
⟦0⟧ is the color of any nation that has very good relations with the nation.
⟦0⟧ is the color of any nations that the nation is currently at war with.
⟦0⟧ is the color of friendly territory that is occupied by enemies.
⟦0⟧ is the color of countries that the nation has wargoals against.
⟦0⟧ is the color of any country the nation has very bad relations with.
⟦0⟧ is the color of any allied nations.

The factions map mode shows the factions that exist around the world. The faction is colored the color of the leader nation, i.e. the Axis is grey due to the color of Germany, and it stretches across all nations in that faction.

The states map mode shows an outline of every state in the world. These outlines are different colors based on the state category which is associated with the quantity of shared building slots. This directly controls how many factories are allowed to be built in a state. The type of state can be found by simply hovering over it.
The infrastructure map mode shows the level of ⟦0⟧ in each state.
The Population map mode shows the amount of ⟦0⟧ in each state.
The Ideology map mode shows the countries by their ⟦0⟧.
⟦0⟧ is the color of communist nations.
⟦0⟧ is the color of democratic nations.
⟦0⟧ is the color of fascist nations.
⟦0⟧ is the color of non-aligned nations.
